1. Open the VMware application and find your virtual machine in the list.

2. Power off the virtual machine if it's currently running, as you won’t be able to change settings while it’s active.

3. Right-click on the virtual machine and select “Settings” or "Edit Settings" from the context menu.

4. Go to the "Advanced" panel or tab within the settings menu.

5. Look for a setting related to CPU or security, which may refer to side channel mitigations.

6. Change the setting from “Enabled” to “Disabled” if you wish to improve performance at the possible cost of increased security risk.

7. Save your changes and restart the virtual machine for the new settings to take effect. 🔄

Remember, disabling security mitigations can expose your system to risk. Make sure to weigh the performance benefits against potential security vulnerabilities. ⚖️

Sure, here's how you can disable side channel mitigations for your virtual machine. 

1. Open your VMware application and locate the virtual machine for which you want to change the settings. 

2. Power off the virtual machine if it's currently running. You can do this by right-clicking on the virtual machine and selecting "Power Off." 

3. Once the virtual machine is powered off, go to the "Edit Virtual Machine Settings" section. 

4. Navigate to the "Advanced" panel of the virtual machine settings. From this panel, you can change the side channel mitigations setting. 

5. Uncheck or modify the setting for side channel mitigations to disable it. This may improve performance at the cost of reduced security against certain vulnerabilities. 

6. Save your changes and close the settings window. 

7. Power on your virtual machine to check if the performance is improved. 

For more detailed instructions, you can refer to the VMware KB article 79832 available at https://kb.vmware.com/s/article/79832.
